statement0:
The word "selection" is mentioned two or more times in 1.8% of psychology papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "selection" , 27.0% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is similar to the typical Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "selection" are in the top 60th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability(see Supplemental Materials 7.3 of the associated paper).
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "selection" tend to be published in higher impact factor journals (91st percentile among all words) and tend to be cited more (76th percentile word). In general, this word is positively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are more likely to publish papers containing "selection" (94th percentile).
